key_insight: Dense Fe-based amorphous coatings with fewer pores show better long-term corrosion resistance, while increasing humidity reduces friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Controlling detonation-spray parameters to minimize coating defects can improve protection of Q235 carbon steel, with service humidity also influencing wear performance.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Examine droplet morphology and coating microstructure.
Evaluate corrosion and tribological behavior under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that greater porosity is associated with lower long-term corrosion resistance and that friction coefficient and wear rate decrease as humidity increases.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative performance gains or humidity ranges, and wear results involve a Si3N4 counterface.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
